stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is working with three support personnel who satisfy the applicable supervisory ratio. A cashier who rings up front-store sales and never assists with prescriptions is also on duty. The Manager of Record asks whether the cashier pushes the pharmacist over the ratio. What is the correct analysis?

choices.text: The cashier is excluded from the ratio because they do not support the pharmacist in a professional capacity.
The cashier counts as a fourth support person and the ratio is exceeded.
The cashier counts unless the pharmacy documents a written exemption.
The cashier counts only during hours when the pharmacy department is open.
The cashier counts as half of a support person for ratio purposes.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.06(3)(b) excludes sales clerks, messengers, delivery personnel, secretaries and other persons who do not fall within the definitions of intern, certified pharmacy technician, pharmacy technician or pharmacy technician trainee, so long as they are not supporting the pharmacist in any professional capacity.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the exclusion turns on the absence of professional support to the pharmacist.
choice_analysis.B: The regulation excludes such staff rather than counting them.
choice_analysis.C: No written exemption mechanism is required for the exclusion to apply.
choice_analysis.D: The exclusion does not depend on the pharmacy department's hours.
choice_analysis.E: The regulation does not use fractional counting.

related_facts: The exclusion is lost if such a person begins supporting the pharmacist professionally.
explanation.mpje_trap: The exclusion depends on what the person actually does, not on their job title alone.

reasoning_steps: Classify the cashier against the four defined support-personnel categories
Test whether the cashier supports the pharmacist in a professional capacity
Apply the exclusion rather than counting the cashier in the ratio
